Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(1,2),$ and passes through the point $(7,-4).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=2pt,\,y-k=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(1,2),$ and so we have

$$
x-1=2pt,\,y-2=p{t}^{2}.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(7,-4),$ we can substitute $x=7$ and $y=-4$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}6=2pt \\ -6=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =2pt \\ t & =\frac{3}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-6 & =p{(\frac{3}{p})}^{2} \\ -6 & =p\cdot \frac{9}{{p}^{2}} \\ -6 & =\frac{9}{p} \\ p & =-\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-1=2(-\frac{3}{2})t,\,y-2=(-\frac{3}{2}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-1=-3t,\,y-2=-\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}.
$$
